external_facts.settled: The obvious command is often the wrong one. Three traps are recorded in the data file and reproduced in the best-practices document: `npm update` stays inside the existing semver ranges and never crosses a major (hence `npm-check-updates -u`, whose default target is the `latest` dist-tag); `cargo update --breaking` is nightly-only, so the stable path is cargo-edit's `cargo upgrade --incompatible`; Maven versions usually live in `<properties>`, so `versions:use-latest-releases` must be paired with `versions:update-properties`.

Exactly 33 values are accepted, and entries are per (ecosystem, directory) pair, so a polyglot repository needs one `updates:` entry per pair. This list is what buildAutomationSection() emits as 'Ecosystems to declare'.
external_facts.caught_a_bug: pnpm is not among the 33. Dependabot covers pnpm-lock.yaml under `npm`, and `package-ecosystem: pnpm` is rejected. DEPENDENCY_ECOSYSTEMS declared it, so the generated issue recommended an invalid dependabot.yml. Fixed in commit 0e01a54c with a regression test that checks every catalog value against this file.

external_facts.settled: Renovate covers more ecosystems and adds grouping and auto-merge rules, but shares the limit that matters here: both are bumpers, not migrators. Neither adapts code to a changed API nor removes a hand-rolled implementation that upstream now provides. Recorded as the alternative in the generated issue's automation section and in the best-practices document.
